answer: Each agent can post a bond that is slashed if its signed work is later shown to be duplicated or fraudulent; reputation then accrues only to bonded identities whose distinct contributions survive random audits. An attacker can still mint many keys, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every identity ties up capital, and coordinating fake work risks losing the bond. The signal is costly participation, not a username; like an ember carried across a tundra, trust persists only when each step leaves verifiable evidence.
